title: Launch Signal Orchestra — Playlist and KPI Runbook
summary: Working runbook that treats launch readiness like an orchestral playlist: discrete, ordered signals (instruments) that must all be "on-key" for go/no-go decisions. Combines a condensed KPI sheet, decision criteria, a three-phase timeline, and an actionable preflight checklist with fallbacks. Purpose: give PMs and Ops a compact single-pane view to run a launch rehearsal and make a clear go/no-go call at T-48, T-12, and T-0.

readiness_checklist:
Preflight (T-72 to T-48):
- Finish canary config and sample traffic ramp (Infra + Serving Runtime).
- Complete security scan of release artifacts (Security).
- Create rollback image and verify rollback test (Release Eng).
- Confirm capacity reservation and autoscale limits for first 72h (Dedicated).
- Prepare support playbook and contact matrix (Customer Success + Support).

Prelaunch (T-48 to T-12):
- Run full dress rehearsal on staging with prod-like traffic profile (SRE + Product Ops).
- Execute load and regression smoke tests; verify KPIs in kpi table.
- Lock model version and artifact hash; freeze rollout policy (Applied ML).
- Publish status page template and alert routing for launch window (Observability).
- Coordinate comms: release notes draft, internal announcement, on-call rotation (GTM + People Ops).

Go decision (T-12 to T-0):
- Confirm canary metrics: latency, error rate, quality score, cost within thresholds.
- Validate fallback policies and automated rollback trigger simulated.
- Stakeholder signoffs: Product, SRE, Security, Finance, Applied ML.
- If any critical threshold breached -> HOLD and follow contingency plan.

Contingency quick actions (if hold):
- Route traffic to previous stable model variant (auto-fallback).
- Revert release artifact and validate preflight tests.
- Throttle traffic or enable degraded mode (read-only or cached responses).
rollout_timeline:
Phase 0 — Canary (T-72 to T-48): 1% traffic -> 5% traffic. Objective: validate basic SLOs and eval quality against canary cohort.
Phase 1 — Ramp (T-48 to T-12): 5% -> 30% over 24h window. Objective: capacity and runtime behavior, billing profile checks.
Phase 2 — Open (T-12 to T+72): 30% -> 100% with staged bursts. Objective: market signals, adoption KPIs, long-tail latency.
Notes: each phase must satisfy the KPI block before progressing; if escalation required, use the decision_criteria to determine pause/rollback.
decision_criteria:
Green (GO): all critical KPIs within thresholds (latency, 5xx, cost within buffer, eval quality >= target), no unresolved P1 or P0 incidents, security signoff present.
Yellow (CAUTION — partial go): one non-critical KPI slightly outside threshold (within 10% over); proceed with limited ramp and increase monitoring cadence; product ops to predefine reduced feature set or throttling.
Red (HOLD/ROLLBACK): any critical KPI breached (error rate > 1.0%, 95th latency > 2x target, token cost runaway > 150% expected) or unresolved security or P0 incident. Immediate rollback to stable variant and incident war room.
risk_matrix:
Risk,Probability(High/Med/Low),Impact(High/Med/Low),Mitigation
Unexpected latency spike,Med,High,Enable autoscale + temporary throttling; prioritize kernel rollbacks and route to dedicated capacity.
Sudden cost surge,Low,High,Predefined per-token caps and alerting; throttle non-essential routes.
Quality regression post-rollout,Med,High,Holdback 10% canary; continuous eval harness post-inference and immediate model rollback path.
Third-party provider outage,Low,Med,Fallback to alternate provider pool and cached responses.
Support overload,Med,Med,Secondary support team backup, public status updates, limited feature mode.
Compliance/legal flag from customer,Low,High,Pause rollout for impacted accounts; escalate to legal and product for remediation.
notes_to_owner: Things to resolve before next iteration: 1) Add an automated dashboard widget for the three canonical go/no-go KPIs so execs can read T-48 decision in one line. 2) Coordinate with Finance to publish expected per-hour token burn estimates for first 48 hours. 3) Run a dry-run rollback drill with SRE within the next two weeks. 4) Capture a short postmortem template to use if any hold occurs (keep it <1 page).
